claims: The Nilsson deformed harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian provides single-particle states characterized in the large prolate deformation limit by asymptotic quantum numbers [N n3 Lambda Omega], with large n3 down-sloping orbits forming unique-parity intruder states (e.g. h11/2, i13/2).
Single-particle states with identical parity pi = (-1)^N and projection Omega undergo avoided crossings that mix spherical j-components c_j.

Single-nucleon transfer reactions (stripping and pickup) yield cross sections proportional to c_j^2 u_nu^2 or c_j^2 v_nu^2, producing distinctive fingerprint patterns that uniquely identify Nilsson orbitals.
In K = 1/2 bands, diagonal Coriolis matrix elements generate the decoupling parameter a, inducing a signature-dependent energy staggering Delta E_1/2(I) = A_rot a (-1)^(I+1/2) (I+1/2).

Second-order Coriolis band mixing renormalizes the rotational parameter delta A through the BCS pairing factor (u_nu u_nu' + v_nu v_nu')^2, with pure Nilsson matrix elements systematically quenched by an empirical attenuation factor of 0.6 - 0.8.

At high spin, Coriolis force -omega j_x decouples the particle from the deformed core, aligning j with the rotational axis to form Stephens rotation-aligned decoupled bands with core-like energy spacings.
